title: Ambient and downtempo
description: Pads, drift, washes and a pulse without a kick: slow music made of space.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: Drift
tracks.blurb: Pads, perlin, washes, a pulse, then a piece.

lessons.title: Pads without drums
lessons.goal: Make a chord that fades in and out instead of hitting.
lessons.concept:
Ambient music (Brian Eno named it, in 1978) is built from sounds that **arrive slowly** and leave slowly. A pad is a chord with a long **attack** (the fade in) and a long **release** (the fade out), so the edges of each note disappear.

A **supersaw** through a closed low-pass filter is the softest pad the site has. Keep the gain low: pads add up.

tasks.text: Give the pad a one-second attack.
And a two-second release, so each chord hangs on.

challenge.text: Alternate two chords, each lasting two bars.
challenge.hint: note("<[c3,eb3,g3,bb3] [ab2,c3,eb3,g3]>").slow(2): angle brackets alternate, .slow(2) stretches each to two bars.

summary: A pad is a chord with a slow attack and a long release.
supersaw + a closed lpf is the softest pad here.

lessons.title: Perlin on everything
lessons.goal: Let smooth randomness move the filter and the stereo image.
lessons.concept:
**Perlin noise** is random but smooth: it wanders rather than jumps. Give it to a control and the sound drifts the way weather does.

`perlin.range(300, 1500).slow(8)` wanders between 300 and 1500 Hz over about eight bars. Put it on `.lpf` and the pad breathes; on `.pan` and it drifts between the speakers. Use different `.slow` values so the movements never line up.

tasks.text: Replace the fixed cutoff with perlin wandering between 300 and 1500 Hz over 8 bars.
Drift the pad between the speakers with perlin on .pan, over 5 bars.

challenge.text: Let the level breathe too: perlin between .3 and .5 on the gain.

summary: perlin is smooth randomness: it wanders.
Different .slow values keep movements out of step.

lessons.title: Washes
lessons.goal: Drown the pad in reverb and a long delay.
lessons.concept:
Ambient space is made of **reverb** turned up past where a mixer would stop, and **delays** whose feedback is so high the echoes become a texture.

`.room(.9)` is a huge hall. A delay of three eighths (`.delaysync(3/8)`) with feedback near .8 repeats for a long time. Keep the pad on its own **orbit** so these settings are the pad’s alone.

tasks.text: A very big reverb on the pad: room .8 or more.
A long delay: three eighths, feedback .8, on its own orbit 2.

challenge.text: Thin the pad out underneath so the wash doesn’t turn to mud: high-pass at 200 Hz.

summary: Reverb and feedback past the usual limits make a wash.
One orbit per part keeps the settings apart.

lessons.title: A pulse without a kick
lessons.goal: Keep time without a drum kit.
lessons.concept:
Downtempo keeps a pulse, but not with a kick drum. A soft **sine** on each beat, short and quiet, is felt more than heard. A single rimshot every other bar is enough rhythm.

The pulse sits in its own space: no reverb, so it stays close while the pad is far away.

tasks.text: Add a part called pulse: a short sine c2 on every beat, quiet.
Add a part called tick: one 606 rimshot on the last 16th of every other bar, in a room.
tasks.hint: const tick = s("<~ [~ ~ ~ rim]>").bank("RolandTR606").gain(.3).room(.6).orbit(3), and stack it.

challenge.text: Let the pulse skip a beat now and then.

summary: A quiet sine on the beat keeps time without drums.
A hit every other bar is plenty.

lessons.title: Project: A drift
lessons.goal: Put a pad, a pulse and the washes together in one key, slowly.
lessons.concept:
Everything from this pack in one piece, at 80 BPM or slower. One `const key` keeps the pad and the pulse in tune. Nothing hits; everything arrives.

If you arrange it, let the pad play alone for the first section: ambient pieces begin with the room, not the beat.

tasks.text: A pad in the key, slow attack and release, with the breathing filter.
Wash it: big room, long delay, its own orbit.
Add the sine pulse on the root, in the key.

challenge.text: Arrange it: 8 bars of pad alone, then 16 with the pulse, then 8 of pad again.
challenge.hint: const intro = stack(pad), const body = stack(pad, pulse), then arrange([8, intro], [16, body], [8, intro]).

steps:
setcpm(80/4)
const key = "C:minor"
const pad = n("[0,2,4,6]").scale(key).s("supersaw").gain(.4).attack(1).release(2).lpf(perlin.range(300, 1500).slow(8))
stack(pad)

setcpm(80/4)
const key = "C:minor"
const pad = n("[0,2,4,6]").scale(key).s("supersaw").gain(.4).attack(1).release(2).lpf(perlin.range(300, 1500).slow(8))
  .room(.9).delay(.6).delaysync(3/8).delayfeedback(.8).orbit(2)
stack(pad)
summary: One key, one pad, one pulse, and a lot of space.
Begin with the room, not the beat.
